pages.text: "I won't sleep! I'll wave my flag!" The train stopped at its final station, but Bami kept waving in the sleeping-car aisle. Sea and sky were dark, stars shining. Holding back a yawn, Bami called, "A little longer!"
Dad entered. "Last stop, Bami. Bedtime." "I'm not sleepy at all!" Bami shook their head and gripped the flag harder.
But their eyes kept closing. The flag slipped from their foot. A huge yawn escaped. "Am I a little sleepy?" Their eyes felt sore.
Dad took Bami to the round window. "When the train stops, lamps go out one by one." On the platform, the bull stationmaster held his flag and blew out a lamp. "Our train gets ready for bed, too!"
First, the dining car. Mom blew out the lamp by the stove and sang softly, "Last stop, sleep tight..." As it grew dark, Bami stood close behind her apron.
Second, the engine cab. Dad blew out the lamp by the big handle. "Last stop, sleep tight..." His voice was warm as a quilt. Darkness wasn't scary; moonlight lay on the sea outside.
Third, the sleeping car. Bami slipped under the soft quilt. Mom touched her beak to their forehead and sang. Only the little bedside lamp remained.
Bami's turn! Standing on the quilt, wings wide, they blew out the little lamp. The whole train was dark; only stars shone in the round window. Blowing out the last light felt good.
The family closed their eyes side by side. Mom, Dad, and Bami. Soft breathing and waves filled the sleeping car. "Last stop, sleep tight..." The song flowed inside Bami's heart.

Morning! The round window was bright. Bami hopped up and shook their feathers, feeling light. Mom cuddled them with her wings. "A good sleep makes the morning sea sparkle!" Now Bami liked bedtime. Last stop, sleep tight!
